intended_object: The canonical natural isomorphism H⁰(id_ℬ) ≅ id between the functor that the identity A∞ functor induces on the cohomological (homotopy) category H⁰(ℬ) of a cohomologically unital A∞ category and the identity functor of H⁰(ℬ). This is the identity part of the functoriality of H⁰. I took this from the docstring and from the surrounding module.
explanation: `mapHomotopyCategory` sends each object X to `ℱ.obj X.obj`. It sends the class of a closed degree-zero morphism f to the class of f₁(f). For the identity A∞ functor, both maps are the identity by definition. So the natural isomorphism is built with `NatIso.ofComponents`, every component is `Iso.refl`, and naturality reduces to `id_map_apply` plus `rfl`. This is exactly the canonical isomorphism H⁰(id) ≅ 𝟭, stated at the generality the library uses for A∞ categories: any commutative ring R and cohomologically unital A∞ categories. The hypothesis that the identity functor is unital is `isUnital_id`, which is a proof, so it adds no restriction. A∞ categories are not in Mathlib, so Mathlib has no counterpart.
